open_points.subject: All validation functions
open_points.text: “raises RefusedError naming the first failing check” and “raise UnknownReferenceError naming …”
open_points.question: What constructor arguments and exact message or payload must be used for RefusedError and UnknownReferenceError?
options: Pass structured identifiers or reason fields
Pass the referenced ID or check enum directly
open_points.default_guess: Pass one descriptive string containing the required ID, port, check, reason, and ceiling where applicable.

open_points.subject: StopRequiredError handling
open_points.text: “then StopRequiredError is raised”
open_points.question: What constructor arguments or message must StopRequiredError receive?
open_points.default_guess: Raise StopRequiredError() without arguments.

open_points.subject: Store query results
open_points.text: “read_records answers” and “returned … from the RecordSet”
open_points.question: When a query or record_change result unexpectedly contains zero or multiple matching records, which record is selected or what error is raised?
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly one where existence is expected and use the sole returned record.

open_points.subject: add_captured_trial_case input references
open_points.text: “values read from their StoredValues … each spooled file of a SpooledFilesRef taken by its SpooledFile facts”
open_points.question: Which PortRef variants are legal in inputs, and what happens for FileFactsRef or any other PortRef variant?
options: Only StoredValuesRef and SpooledFilesRef are legal
Allow FileFactsRef as an already materialized file
Pass every variant through a generic conversion
open_points.default_guess: Accept only StoredValuesRef and SpooledFilesRef and refuse other variants as a carriage failure.

open_points.subject: add_captured_trial_case input structure
open_points.text: “then each input port in port name order does not fit by fit_port_value”
open_points.question: How are extra names, duplicate names, missing ports, multiple StoredValuesRef entries, and references of the wrong cardinality detected and ordered before fit checks?
options: Prevalidate names in supplied order as add_trial_case does
Aggregate by port and let fit_port_value report presence or carriage in port order
open_points.default_guess: Reject unknown and repeated scalar references in supplied order, then aggregate and fit every contract input in port-name order.

open_points.subject: add_captured_trial_case source
open_points.text: “origin captured and captured_from the given source”
open_points.question: Must each SpooledFileKey belong to the supplied AttemptKey, and must that attempt show that executed_implementation_id was actually executed?
options: Validate only spool keys against the source
Treat source as provenance metadata only
open_points.default_guess: Treat source as provenance metadata only because no such relationship check is specified.

open_points.subject: add_captured_trial_case referenced records
open_points.text: “values read from their StoredValues … taken by its SpooledFile facts”
open_points.question: What error and ordering apply when a StoredValue ID or SpooledFileKey does not exist?
options: Refuse the input as a fit failure
open_points.default_guess: Propagate UnknownReferenceError while resolving references in port-name and file-list order.

open_points.subject: add_captured_trial_case stored values
open_points.text: “every input becomes a StoredValue … values keeping their value_digest and files becoming file-carriage StoredValues for the copied digests”
open_points.question: For an existing StoredValuesRef, is a new StoredValueContent/value_id always created using the contract port schema and class, or is the referenced StoredValue reused?
options: Reuse only when schema and class already match
open_points.default_guess: Create a new StoredValue descriptor with the contract port schema and disclosure class while retaining digest and size.

open_points.subject: add_captured_trial_case equality path
open_points.text: “the equal existing one unchanged when its trial_case_id exists” and “Only after every check passed, each spooled file's bytes are … published with put_value_bytes”
open_points.question: Must existence of the equal TrialCase be checked before publishing copied spool bytes, so that the equal-case path performs no value-store writes?
options: Publish bytes before checking case existence
open_points.default_guess: Check for the existing case after validation but before copying any bytes.

open_points.subject: add_trial_case payload variants
open_points.text: “each input value becomes a StoredValue” and “a file candidate taking the payload's digest, size and the port's media type”
open_points.question: Which concrete PortPayload type is legal for each carriage/cardinality combination, especially a many value port?
options: JsonPayload for all value ports, with an array document for many; FilePayload/FileListPayload for file ports
Introduce one payload per many value item
Let fit_port_value accept any payload shape
open_points.default_guess: Use one JsonPayload for a value port, including a JSON array for cardinality many, and FilePayload or FileListPayload for file ports.

open_points.subject: add_trial_case duplicate names
open_points.text: “the first name in inputs that is not an input port … or repeats an earlier name”
open_points.question: Does a many file port appear once as a FileListPayload, or may it repeat as multiple FilePayload entries despite the duplicate-name rule?
options: It must appear once as FileListPayload
Repeated FilePayload entries are allowed for many files
open_points.default_guess: Require one FileListPayload for a many file port.

open_points.subject: Stored value digesting
open_points.text: “value_digest is content_identity of the bytes”
open_points.question: Which IdentitySubject wrapper is used to pass bytes to content_identity?
options: Pass raw bytes despite the declared signature
JsonTextContent for JSON and BytesContent for files
open_points.default_guess: Use BytesContent for every byte sequence.

open_points.subject: Stored schema M21
open_points.text: “the port's value_schema, or for a many port the canonical array schema with it as items”
open_points.question: What exact JSON serialization defines the canonical array schema, including key ordering and whitespace?
options: Preserve formatting from the original schema inside a template
open_points.default_guess: Parse the schema and serialize {"items":schema,"type":"array"} with sorted keys and compact separators.

open_points.subject: add_trial_case existing case
open_points.text: “an existing equal case is returned with its first place and nothing is written” and “the bytes are stored with put_value_bytes”
open_points.question: Must trial-case existence be checked before all put_value_bytes calls?
options: Compute all identities and check the case before storing bytes
Store bytes first, then check the case
open_points.default_guess: Compute descriptors and case identity in memory, check for the case, and only then call put_value_bytes.

open_points.subject: admit_implementation kernel actor
open_points.text: “MUST act as the kernel actor”
open_points.question: What exact Actor value represents the kernel, particularly agent_name?
open_points.default_guess: Use Actor(kind='kernel', agent_name=None).

open_points.subject: admit_implementation existing verdict
open_points.text: “when a verdict over the current corpus digest exists for the implementation it is reused”
open_points.question: If multiple matching verdicts exist, which one is reused?
open_points.default_guess: Reuse the latest matching verdict in store order.

open_points.subject: admit_implementation execution side effects
open_points.text: “A StopRequiredError … no verdict and no activation are written”
open_points.question: Are TrialExecution records successfully written before the cleanup failure intentionally retained, or must the whole admission be atomic?
options: Roll back all executions in the admission request
open_points.default_guess: Retain already recorded TrialExecutions because execute_trial_case explicitly records each one and no transactional rollback is specified.

open_points.subject: current_activation
open_points.text: “MUST raise UnknownReferenceError … when it does not exist” and “return the Activation that a LatestActivationOfContractVersion query … answers”
open_points.question: Must contract-version existence be queried separately before the activation query, or is an empty activation result sufficient to distinguish unknown from inactive?
options: Use one activation query that also signals existence
open_points.default_guess: Call read_contract_version first, then query the latest activation.

open_points.subject: execute_trial_case inputs
open_points.text: “MUST read the case's input bytes with read_value_bytes, build one PortPayload per input port”
open_points.question: How are TrialCase PortRefs grouped and mapped to ports if their stored order is malformed, duplicated, missing, or includes a non-StoredValuesRef?
open_points.default_guess: Trust stored TrialCase invariants and resolve StoredValuesRef entries in recorded order.

open_points.subject: execute_trial_case byte sources
open_points.text: “read the case's input bytes with read_value_bytes”
open_points.question: What ByteSource is used for each StoredValuesRef?
options: A source derived from the StoredValue digest
open_points.default_guess: Use StoredValueSource for every StoredValuesRef.

open_points.subject: execute_trial_case sandbox outputs
open_points.text: “a succeeded execution is passed when … every output's digest equals the expected one”
open_points.question: What happens if a succeeded SandboxResult has missing, extra, duplicate, wrongly named, wrongly typed, or wrongly ordered output payloads?
open_points.default_guess: Treat malformed output structure or carriage as contract_violation.

open_points.subject: execute_trial_case output ordering
open_points.text: “For passed and output_mismatch the outputs are recorded”
open_points.question: Are recorded output refs ordered by contract output name, contract declaration order, or SandboxResult order?
open_points.default_guess: Use Unicode port-name order for deterministic records.

open_points.subject: execute_trial_case expected output lookup
open_points.text: “every output's digest equals the expected one”
open_points.question: For value outputs, is equality based only on value_digest, or must schema, carriage, media type, and cardinality also match?
open_points.default_guess: Compare digests as stated, after treating structurally invalid sandbox output as contract_violation.

open_points.subject: execute_trial_case file digest
open_points.text: “a file by digest, size and media type only as a FileFactsRef”
open_points.question: How is a sandbox file output's digest computed from FilePayload bytes?
open_points.default_guess: Use content_identity(BytesContent(...)).

open_points.subject: execute_trial_case file persistence
open_points.text: “a file by digest, size and media type only as a FileFactsRef”
open_points.question: Are sandbox file-output bytes deliberately not passed to put_value_bytes, and if so where can those FileFactsRef bytes later be read from?
options: Persist them with put_value_bytes despite saying facts only
open_points.default_guess: Do not call put_value_bytes for file outputs because the requirement explicitly says facts only.

open_points.subject: execute_trial_case oversized values
open_points.text: “a succeeded value output whose canonical bytes exceed … makes the outcome contract_violation”
open_points.question: If one output is oversized, must all outputs be size-checked before any earlier output bytes are stored, and which oversized port wins if several fail?
options: Precheck all in deterministic port order before writes
Process sequentially and allow earlier writes
open_points.default_guess: Precheck outputs in Unicode port-name order and perform no output storage when any is oversized.

open_points.subject: execute_trial_case detail fields
open_points.text: “detail_code (value_too_large for an output over the stored value ceiling), the sandbox's failure_detail”
open_points.question: For a locally detected oversized output, is sandbox failure_detail retained, cleared, or replaced, and is an existing sandbox detail_code always overridden?
open_points.default_guess: Override detail_code with value_too_large and retain the sandbox failure_detail.

open_points.subject: execute_trial_case cleanup failure
open_points.text: “When the sandbox reports detail cleanup_failed the execution is recorded crashed with detail_code cleanup_failed first”
open_points.question: Does cleanup_failed override every SandboxOutcome, including succeeded, timeout, or contract_violation?
open_points.default_guess: Always override the outcome to crashed.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version schema representation
open_points.text: “A supported value_schema is a JSON object” while Port.value_schema is “str”
open_points.question: Must value_schema be parsed from JSON text, and are malformed JSON and non-object JSON refused as unsupported schema?
options: Parse the string and require an object
Treat the string itself as the schema value
open_points.default_guess: Parse it as JSON and refuse malformed or non-object values.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version schema grammar
open_points.text: “using only type as one string … enum … const … properties and required for object … items … minItems …”
open_points.question: Is type mandatory, and which keywords are required or allowed conditionally for each type?
options: type is mandatory and type-specific keywords are allowed only for their type
type is optional and any listed keyword may coexist
open_points.default_guess: Require type and permit listed constraints only where they apply to that type.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version schema constraints
open_points.text: “enum as a non-empty array of distinct scalars … minItems, maxItems, minLength, maxLength, minimum and maximum”
open_points.question: What counts as a scalar and distinct value, and must min/max constraints have particular numeric types, be nonnegative, and satisfy minimum ≤ maximum?
options: Use strict JSON-type equality and validate all natural boundaries
Use Python equality and accept any numeric limits
open_points.default_guess: Use strict JSON scalar types, reject booleans as numbers, require nonnegative integer lengths/counts, and require each minimum not exceed its maximum.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version object schemas
open_points.text: “properties and required for object”
open_points.question: Are properties and required mandatory, what are their exact container types, must required names be distinct strings, and must every required name exist in properties?
options: Both mandatory with required a unique subset of property names
Both optional but validated when present
open_points.default_guess: Allow both to be optional; when present require properties to map strings to supported schemas and required to be a unique list of property names present in properties.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version enum and const
open_points.text: “enum … const … nested schemas following the same rule”
open_points.question: Must enum/const values conform to type and other constraints, and may enum and const appear together?
options: Validate consistency and allow together only when compatible
open_points.default_guess: Validate them against type and allow both only when const is one of the enum values.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version file schema
open_points.text: “a file port's value_schema is the empty object”
open_points.question: Does this require the exact string "{}", or any JSON text that parses to an empty object?
options: Any JSON serialization of an empty object
open_points.default_guess: Accept any string parsing to an empty JSON object.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version port validation
open_points.text: “ports are taken inputs first then outputs, each by name”
open_points.question: Must every port's direction agree with the tuple it appears in, and are empty port names or the same name used once in each direction permitted?
options: Validate direction, allow cross-direction duplicates and empty names
Validate direction and globally unique nonempty names
Perform only the explicitly listed checks
open_points.default_guess: Validate direction against its tuple, allow the same name across directions, and do not invent a nonempty-name rule.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version port order
open_points.text: “ports are taken inputs first then outputs, each by name”
open_points.question: Are inputs and outputs sorted by Unicode name before constructing ContractVersionContent, or is caller-supplied order preserved after checks?
options: Sort each direction before identity construction
open_points.default_guess: Sort each direction by Unicode code point before constructing content.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version purpose
open_points.text: “a new slot_id with purpose None, or an existing slot whose purpose differs from a given purpose”
open_points.question: For an existing slot with purpose=None, is that accepted as meaning no requested change, and are empty slot IDs or empty purposes valid?
options: None accepts the existing purpose; empty strings are valid
None conflicts with the existing purpose
open_points.default_guess: Treat None as no purpose assertion for an existing slot and allow empty strings because no prohibition is stated.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version ID timing
open_points.text: “contract_version_id is computed right after the purpose rule” but ResourceBoundsRequest fields may be None and “a resource bound that is None … is refused” only in a later check
open_points.question: How can ContractVersionContent and ResourceBounds be constructed for identity before validating or converting nullable bounds?
options: Validate non-null/type enough to construct bounds before computing ID, deferring ceiling checks
Construct ResourceBounds with invalid None values
Compute an identity from ResourceBoundsRequest instead
open_points.default_guess: Perform the minimum non-null integer conversion needed to construct ResourceBounds before identity calculation, then defer positivity and ceiling rejection for a new version.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version resource integers
open_points.text: “not a positive integer”
open_points.question: Does Python bool count as an integer, and are integer subclasses accepted?
options: Reject booleans and accept integral integers
Accept bool because it is an int
open_points.default_guess: Reject booleans and accept ordinary positive integers.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version existing version
open_points.text: “an existing equal contract version is returned unchanged even when a later release lowered a ceiling below its bounds”
open_points.question: Which later checks besides release ceilings are skipped for an existing identity—schema checks, port checks, no-output checks, and positivity checks as well?
options: Skip ceilings but still enforce intrinsic validity
open_points.default_guess: Skip every check after purpose once an equal contract_version_id is found, as the prompt explicitly says every later check binds only a new version.

open_points.subject: read_corpus note
open_points.text: “The corpus of a contract version is its trial cases in store order, read through read_corpus”
open_points.question: Is “read through read_corpus” intended to name the owned function recursively, or should it say read_records with CorpusOfContractVersion?
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a wording error and use read_records with CorpusOfContractVersion.

open_points.subject: read_corpus unknown contract
open_points.text: “an empty tuple for an empty corpus”
open_points.question: Does an unknown contract_version_id raise UnknownReferenceError or also return an empty tuple?
open_points.default_guess: Raise UnknownReferenceError after checking the contract version, distinguishing unknown from an empty corpus.

open_points.subject: read_slot current corpus digest
open_points.text: “per contract version … its current corpus digest”
open_points.question: Must read_slot recompute the digest as content_identity(CorpusContent(...)), or is it expected to obtain a precomputed digest from a query result?
options: Read a stored digest from an unspecified record
open_points.default_guess: Recompute it from trial_case_ids in corpus order.

open_points.subject: read_slot query and ordering
open_points.text: “per contract version in store order its … implementations in store order each with its verdicts in store order”
open_points.question: Which read_records queries must be issued, and should returned tuple order always be trusted or explicitly sorted by store_position when most listed records expose no store_position field?
open_points.default_guess: Use the corresponding collection queries and trust their returned tuple order as store order.

open_points.subject: read_slot current version
open_points.text: “current_contract_version_id the slot's contract version latest in store order”
open_points.question: What happens if a stored Slot has no ContractVersion records, although SlotHistory requires a string ID?
options: Treat it as impossible store corruption
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an impossible store invariant and raise an error rather than fabricate an ID.

open_points.subject: roll_back_slot admitted verdict selection
open_points.text: “when it holds no admitted verdict over the current corpus digest”
open_points.question: If several verdicts exist for that digest, does any admitted verdict suffice even if a later refused verdict exists?
open_points.default_guess: Any admitted verdict over the digest suffices, matching “holds an admitted verdict.”

open_points.subject: roll_back_slot current activation shortcut
open_points.text: “when the implementation is the current activation, MUST return that Activation without any further check”
open_points.question: Does the shortcut occur only after verifying that the implementation belongs to the slot's current contract version, as the preceding order says, even for stale serving activations?
options: Return any matching current activation before membership
open_points.default_guess: Perform the stated slot, implementation, and current-contract membership checks before the shortcut.

open_points.subject: submit_implementation identity collision
open_points.text: “an equal existing one writes nothing and is read from the store and used unchanged”
open_points.question: If the implementation_id exists but stored content is not equal, is this treated as impossible, refused, or silently reused?
open_points.default_guess: Treat a same-ID/different-content record as an integrity failure.

open_points.subject: try_implementation validation phases
open_points.text: “raise UnknownReferenceError for the first named case that does not exist, then RefusedError naming the first named case that belongs to another contract version or is named twice”
open_points.question: Must all IDs be scanned for unknown cases before checking any earlier contract mismatch or duplicate, or are all checks applied case-by-case?
options: Two full phases: all unknown checks, then mismatch/duplicate checks
open_points.default_guess: Use two phases, so any unknown named case is reported before every mismatch or duplicate.

open_points.subject: try_implementation empty corpus
open_points.text: “then RefusedError with reason empty_corpus when the corpus is empty” and “execute the named cases, or every case when none is named”
open_points.question: Is empty_corpus checked only when trial_case_ids is empty, or unconditionally after named-case validation?
options: Check only when defaulting to all corpus cases
open_points.default_guess: Check the implementation contract's corpus unconditionally after named-case validation.

open_points.subject: try_implementation execution order
open_points.text: “MUST execute the named cases … in corpus order”
open_points.question: If named cases are a subset, is their order determined by their positions in the current corpus even when trial_case_ids are supplied in another order?
open_points.default_guess: Filter the current corpus by the named ID set and execute in corpus order.
